why: Sudoku is choose, explore, un-choose with heavy pruning: put a digit in an empty cell only if its row, column and box do not already hold it, recurse, and erase it if the rest cannot be completed.
hints: Fill the empty cells one at a time. Which digits are legal for a cell, and what do you do when none is?
Keep sets (or bitmasks) of used digits per row, column and box. For a cell, try each digit absent from all three, add it, recurse, and remove it if the recursion fails.
Prune harder by always filling the empty cell with the fewest legal digits next. Return the board once no empty cell remains.
pitfalls: Undo all three set updates when you backtrack, not just the board cell.
